newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil actor convicted in soap opera murder.
newsitem.headline: Brazil actor convicted in soap opera murder.

text.p: Brazil on Saturday concluded act one of its sensational soap opera murder trial with the conviction of a male-stripper-turned-television-star accused of stabbing his screen lover to death.
After all-night deliberations and summing up, a jury found 27-year-old Guilherme de Padua guilty of the 1992 killing of co-star Daniella Perez.
The judge, labeling the defendant "perverse, violent and cowardly," sentenced de Padua to 19 years in jail, of which he has already served four while awaiting trial.
"This is unfair. The cards were marked from the start," de Padua said as he was led to prison by armed guards, according to images transmitted by Globo television.
De Padua was accused jointly with his former wife Paula Thomaz, aged 23. She still has to stand trial separately at a date yet to be determined.
The killing of Perez, then 22, has gripped millions of Brazilian soap opera fans and at the time even outshone the ongoing impeachment of former President Fernando Collor.
Many have watched its twists and turns as closely as the soap opera, "De Corpo e Alma" (Of Body and Soul), in which de Padua and his victim starred.
De Padua shot to fame as the brooding lover of sexy teenager Yasmin, played by Perez.

The case, littered with interviews by the defendants from behind bars, conflicting testimony from limelight-seeking witnesses and angry calls for justice from the victim's family, was Brazil's equivalent of America's O.J. Simpson trial.
De Padua originally confessed to the crime, saying Perez had been hounding him to have sex with her. Later, after his divorce from Thomaz, he accused her.
During his testimony, de Padua said Thomaz carried out the murder in a fit of jealousy, stabbing Perez at least 15 times with a pair of scissors.
He said he had had an affair with Perez because her mother, Gloria, was the script writer for the soap opera and it was in his "interests" to keep on her good side.
Gloria Perez told reporters she was relieved that de Padua had paid the price for the "lies he told about my daughter." But she added: "Nothing can bring her back!"

Many observers of the trial noted that de Padua's testimony was probably his best bit of acting ever. The proceedings, carried exclusively by national CBN radio, sounded like a scene from the soap opera.
The trial has taken place under an intense media spotlight, the courthouse packed with television crews and journalists.
As the judge read out his judgment at 8 a.m. (1000 GMT), television crews tried to push into the courtroom and a fight erupted with security guards. A crew from Globo was arrested.

Outside, protesters demanding justice had been camping for days, including womens' rights groups that sprang up after the murder and pressure groups demanding an overhaul of Brazil's justice system, where prominent defendants often go free.
